title.en: Much as I admire the plan
title.es: Por mucho que admire el plan

es: Formar concesivas avanzadas con much as, however + adjetivo y adjetivo + as/though en lugar de although.

vocabulary.es: a pesar de que, pese a lo mucho que

teaching.en: Much as I admire the council's ambition, I cannot back a scheme that comes with a hefty fee.
teaching.es: Por mucho que admire la ambición del municipio, no puedo respaldar un plan que trae consigo una cuota abultada.
teaching.explanationEs: Much as + sujeto + verbo = «por mucho que»; el verbo va en indicativo y la postura sigue sin but.
segments: Much as I admire the council's ambition, I cannot
back a scheme that comes with a hefty fee.
teaching.audioText: Much as I admire the council's ambition, I cannot back a scheme that comes with a hefty fee.

teaching.en: However tempting the free trial may be, nobody should be swayed by it before reading the small print.
teaching.es: Por muy tentadora que sea la prueba gratuita, nadie debería dejarse influir por ella antes de leer la letra pequeña.
teaching.explanationEs: However + adjetivo + sujeto + verbo; may be añade posibilidad («por muy tentadora que pueda ser»).
segments: However tempting the free trial may be, nobody should
be swayed by it before reading the small print.
teaching.audioText: However tempting the free trial may be, nobody should be swayed by it before reading the small print.

teaching.en: Strict though the new rules may seem, they have one clear advantage: nobody can claim they were applied unfairly.
teaching.es: Por estrictas que parezcan las nuevas normas, tienen una ventaja clara: nadie puede alegar que se aplicaron injustamente.
teaching.explanationEs: Adjetivo + though + sujeto + verbo: el adjetivo pasa al principio; puedes cambiar though por as.
segments: Strict though the new rules may seem, they have one
clear advantage: nobody can claim they were applied unfairly.
teaching.audioText: Strict though the new rules may seem, they have one clear advantage: nobody can claim they were applied unfairly.

teaching.en: Clever as the proposal is, it has a fatal flaw: it depends on every household paying on time.
teaching.es: Por ingeniosa que sea la propuesta, tiene un defecto fatal: depende de que todos los hogares paguen a tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: Con as el adjetivo también va delante, y la segunda parte no lleva but.
segments: Clever as the proposal is, it has a fatal
flaw: it depends on every household paying on time.
teaching.audioText: Clever as the proposal is, it has a fatal flaw: it depends on every household paying on time.

teaching.en: However much effort the staff put in, the plan will come at a cost that somebody must pay.
teaching.es: Por mucho esfuerzo que haga el personal, el plan tendrá un precio que alguien deberá pagar.
teaching.explanationEs: However much + nombre + sujeto + verbo = «por mucho… que»; come at a cost significa tener un precio, salir caro.
segments: However much effort the staff put in, the plan
will come at a cost that somebody must pay.
teaching.audioText: However much effort the staff put in, the plan will come at a cost that somebody must pay.

teaching.en: Tempting as the trip was, Mia turned it down; for all that she admired the organisers, the fee was too steep.
teaching.es: Aunque el viaje era tentador, Mia lo rechazó; pese a lo mucho que admiraba a los organizadores, la cuota era excesiva.
teaching.explanationEs: For all that + sujeto + verbo = «a pesar de que», con tono formal; en pasado la estructura funciona igual.
segments: Tempting as the trip was, Mia turned it down; for all
that she admired the organisers, the fee was too steep.
teaching.audioText: Tempting as the trip was, Mia turned it down; for all that she admired the organisers, the fee was too steep.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por mucho que valoremos la biblioteca, no podemos pagar la cuota.»

answer.text: Much as we value the library we cannot pay the fee
accepted: Much as we value the library we cannot pay the fee
We cannot pay the fee much as we value the library

feedback.es: Much as + sujeto + verbo abre la concesión y la postura sigue sin but; el orden inverso también es natural.

hint.es: Empieza por Much as y no añadas but.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por pequeña que suene, sigue siendo una subida del veinte por ciento.»

feedback.es: Tras However va el adjetivo, luego el sujeto y el verbo: However small it may sound equivale a «por pequeña que suene».

hint.es: Va delante del adjetivo y significa «por muy… que».

origin.text: The bus company calls the new fare a small adjustment. ___ small it may sound, it is still a rise of twenty per cent for people on low incomes.

prompt.es: Elige la frase bien formada con adjetivo + though.

choices.text: Generous though sounds the offer, it comes at a cost.
Generous though the offer sounds, it comes at a cost.
Though generous the offer sounds, but it comes at a cost.

feedback.es: El adjetivo abre la frase y le siguen though, el sujeto y el verbo, sin invertir el orden ni añadir but.

hint.es: Tras though viene el sujeto y luego el verbo; la segunda parte no lleva but.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la actitud de la hablante hacia el plan de la biblioteca.

choices.text: Content with the plan, since she expects the council to cover the repairs.
On the side of the architects, who she feels have been unfairly blamed for the cost.
Admiring of the library, yet worried about who will meet the repair bills.

feedback.es: La hablante concede la admiración con «Much as…», pero lo que destaca es la preocupación por el coste y por quién pagará las reparaciones; ni confía en que el municipio pague ni defiende a los arquitectos.

origin.audio: Much as the residents admire the new library, they cannot ignore what it will cost them. However popular the plan is, it will raise their bills by eight per cent. Generous though the architects have been, and for all that the building is lovely, nobody has explained who will pay for the repairs.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por mucho dinero que recaude, el techo no se reparará antes del invierno.»

feedback.es: However much + nombre no contable (money) equivale a «por mucho dinero que»; con nombres contables usarías however many.

origin.text: The club has worked hard all year. However ___ money it raises, the roof will not be repaired before winter.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por ingenioso que sea el plan, tendrá un precio.»

answer.text: However clever the plan is it will come at a cost
accepted: However clever the plan is it will come at a cost
It will come at a cost however clever the plan is

feedback.es: However clever va pegado delante del sujeto the plan; después el verbo is cierra la concesión.

prompt.es: Escucha la noticia y elige por qué la líder rechaza conservar la piscina vieja.

choices.text: Repairing the old building would cost far more than replacing it.
The volunteers had stopped looking after the old building.
The council had already promised money for a new pool elsewhere.
The pool had been losing money for several years already.

feedback.es: La líder lo dice con «however much effort…»: los arreglos costarían más que una piscina nueva; el resto reinterpreta datos que no aparecen o que ella contradice.

origin.audio: At last night's meeting about the swimming pool, the council leader spoke first. Much as she admired the volunteers who had kept the old building open, she said, the roof was beyond repair, and however much effort they put in, the repairs would cost more than a new pool. Tempting as it was to keep the old one for sentimental reasons, she could not recommend it. A resident then rose to answer. Small though the pool was, he said, it was the only one within ten miles, and for all that the figures looked convincing, nobody had asked the families who use it. The leader thanked him, promised nothing, and closed the meeting.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué sugiere el final de la noticia sobre la decisión de la líder?

choices.text: She has been persuaded and will now reopen the old pool.
She has heard his point without committing to change her plan.
She is annoyed by his remarks and rejects everything he said.
She will ask the families who use the pool before voting.

feedback.es: La líder le da las gracias pero «promised nothing»: reconoce el argumento sin comprometerse a cambiar de plan; no dice que consultará ni que se haya convencido.

origin.audio: At last night's meeting about the swimming pool, the council leader spoke first. Much as she admired the volunteers who had kept the old building open, she said, the roof was beyond repair, and however much effort they put in, the repairs would cost more than a new pool. Tempting as it was to keep the old one for sentimental reasons, she could not recommend it. A resident then rose to answer. Small though the pool was, he said, it was the only one within ten miles, and for all that the figures looked convincing, nobody had asked the families who use it. The leader thanked him, promised nothing, and closed the meeting.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mia se negó a dejarse influir por la prueba gratuita y leyó la letra pequeña.»

feedback.es: Be swayed by es la colocación para dejarse influir por algo; tempted o persuaded también son posibles en este contexto.

origin.text: Mia refused to be ___ by the free trial. It looked generous, but she read the small print before she signed anything.

prompt.es: Reescribe con Much as en lugar de Although.

answer.text: Much as I admire the ambition, I think the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.
accepted: Much as I admire the ambition, I think the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.
Much as I admire the ambition I think the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.
Much as I admire the ambition, I believe the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.

feedback.es: Although + sujeto + verbo pasa a Much as + sujeto + verbo y el resto de la frase se mantiene, sin but.

origin.text: Although I admire the ambition, I think the plan will come at a cost that families cannot afford.

evidenceGroups: much as i admire the ambition
the plan will come at a cost

prompt.es: ¿Qué pretende lograr esta carta de los vecinos al municipio?

choices.text: To reject the proposal as clever in theory but unrealistic in practice.
To praise the committee's goodwill as the real answer to the funding gap.
To obtain a change to the payment terms instead of rejecting the plan.
To persuade residents to vote against any new fee that the council proposes.

feedback.es: Los vecinos reconocen el ingenio del plan, señalan el defecto y piden repartir el pago: buscan cambiar las condiciones, no rechazarlo.

origin.text: Dear councillors, clever as the proposal is, it has a flaw that we cannot overlook. It assumes that every household can pay the new fee in a single payment, and however much goodwill there is on the committee, goodwill will not cover the gap for families on low incomes. We therefore ask the council to spread the payment over twelve months before any vote is taken.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Aunque admiraba el plan, votó en contra.»

answer.text: For all that she admired the plan she voted against it
accepted: For all that she admired the plan she voted against it
She voted against it for all that she admired the plan

feedback.es: For all that + sujeto + verbo equivale a «a pesar de que» y abre la concesión antes de la decisión.

prompt.es: Completa: «La subida de este año es considerable: casi el doble del precio anterior.»

feedback.es: Hefty es el adjetivo habitual para una cuota o subida grande; steep o substantial también encajan aquí.

origin.text: Families have paid the membership fee for years without complaint. This year's rise, however, is a ___ one: nearly double the old price.
